messages:
carl: heads up — seeing periodic cudaMalloc spikes on prod-dedicated-2, ~3-4s stalls, recurring every ~90s. Perfetto trace: https://perfetto.app/trace/... (private). nsys archive uploaded to S3 s3://redwood-traces/2069987654/nsys.qdrep. nvtx regions show lots of 'kv_cache:evict' then immediate cudaMalloc calls.
maya: can you paste the NVTX names you see? is this aligned with the batching rollout last week?
carl: NVTX snippets: "kv_cache:lookup", "kv_cache:evict", "arena:commit_slab", then a cascade of cuMemAlloc/CUDA API calls. The timeline shows small kernels sandwiched between host-side cudaMallocs.
sam: quick hypothesis: small-allocation storm from KV cache misses + adaptive-batcher change -> arena exhausted -> fallback to cudaMalloc. We rolled adaptive-batcher v2 on 2026-03-10, right?
diane: yes we did. v2 reduced latency at low qps but changed avg seq distribution on the fast path. If slab targets are tuned to the old distribution, we could be reallocating more often.
carl: repro plan: run bench_client with the same seq dist. Command I used: \`./bench_client --model llama2-70b --concurrency 8 --qps 250 --seq-dist zipf:1.3 --prefix-cache=128MB\`. Stress run shows alloc spikes align with prefix-cache churn.
maya: try staging with ARENA_SLAB_TARGET=32MB and ARENA_MIN_CHUNKS=4. Also enable ALLOC_TRACE to get stackshots: \`export ALLOC_TRACE=1; ./server --config ...\` so nsys will annotate alloc callsites.
diane: also add metric kvcache.alloc_fallback_rate to backend so we can alert before user-visible stalls. Threshold suggestion: 0.5% over 5m.
perf-bot: automated note: kernel-selector config change detected in canary on 2026-03-10. If rollback needed, submit config rollback PR referencing #2069987654.
carl: did a staging run with ARENA_SLAB_TARGET=32MB and prealloc enabled: spikes dropped from ~3s to <50ms. Perfetto flame shows no cudaMalloc waterfall now. Upload: https://perfetto.app/trace/2069987654/staging
sam: opened PR 5123 to increase slab target & enable async prealloc by default for dedicated pools. Added test harness to reproduce alloc fallback: \`tests/alloc_stress.py --users 40 --seq-zipf 1.3\`.
diane: plan for rollout: canary for 2h, monitor kvcache.alloc_fallback_rate and cudaMalloc-time p99. If fallback_rate > 0.5% or cudaMalloc p99 > 200ms, rollback.
carl: thanks — will run canary tomorrow morning and paste nsys snapshots. if anyone has a reproducer with smaller infra footprint, drop it here.
